senses.gloss: General discussion of a question that people disagree about.
examples: There is still *debate* about how the fire started.
The proposal set off fierce *debate* among the neighbors.
Whether the law actually helped remains open to *debate*.

senses.gloss: An obligation to someone who has helped you.
examples: I owe her a *debt* of gratitude for taking me in.
He said he had paid his *debt* to society.
We are in your *debt* for everything you did that winter.

senses.gloss: A slow decline of a place, an institution, or standards.
examples: Whole blocks of the city fell into *decay* after the plant closed.
The novel traces the *decay* of a once-proud family.
Critics blamed the schools' *decay* on years of budget cuts.

senses.gloss: A complete set of playing cards.
examples: Shuffle the *deck* and deal seven cards each.
He keeps a *deck* of cards in the glove box.
Two of the *decks* were missing a queen.

senses.gloss: One of the floors of a ship, especially the open top one.
examples: Passengers gathered on the *deck* to watch the harbor.
The lower *decks* were already flooded.
She went up on *deck* for some air.

senses.gloss: A person or thing used to lure someone into a trap or draw attention away.
examples: The parked van was a *decoy* while the real truck slipped out the back.
Police used an unmarked car as a *decoy*.
The fake email was a *decoy* to get her password.

senses.gloss: Something that someone does, especially something notable.
examples: She was honored for her good *deeds* in the community.
He is remembered for one brave *deed*.
Words matter less than *deeds*.

senses.gloss: The setting or option a system uses until someone changes it.
senses.ru: значение по умолчанию, настройка по умолчанию
examples: The browser's *default* is to block pop-ups.
You can change the *default* in the settings menu.
Leave it at the *default* if you are not sure.

senses.gloss: The number of points a team or player is behind by.
examples: They erased a twelve-point *deficit* in the fourth quarter.
The team faced a two-goal *deficit* at halftime.
It was too big a *deficit* to overcome in ten minutes.

senses.gloss: A shortage of something that is needed.
examples: The town has a serious *deficit* of affordable housing.
There is a *deficit* of trust between the two sides.
Sleep *deficits* build up over the week.

senses.gloss: A qualification given by a university to a student who completes a course of study.
senses.ru: учёная степень, диплом о высшем образовании
examples: She has a *degree* in civil engineering.
He finished his *degree* at night school.
Both *degrees* hang framed in her office.

senses.gloss: A unit for measuring angles, of which a full circle has 360.
examples: Turn the panel ninety *degrees* to the left.
The ramp rises at an angle of about ten *degrees*.
A right angle is exactly 90 *degrees*.

senses.gloss: The amount or extent to which something is true or present.
examples: There is a *degree* of risk in any investment.
To some *degree*, we were all responsible.
The work requires a high *degree* of accuracy.

senses.gloss: A personal problem or painful memory that torments someone.
examples: He spent years fighting his *demons*.
Getting sober meant facing her *demons*.
The book is about a writer wrestling with old *demons*.

senses.gloss: A refusal to give someone something they have asked for.
examples: The insurance company sent a *denial* of her claim.
He is appealing the *denial* of his visa.
Repeated *denials* of parole kept him in prison.

senses.gloss: How many people or things there are in a given area.
examples: The city has the highest population *density* in the state.
Traffic *density* doubles during the morning rush.
New zoning rules allow greater *density* downtown.

senses.gloss: A noticeable reduction in an amount or a problem.
examples: The bonus barely made a *dent* in our debt.
A week of work put a real *dent* in the backlog.
The new clinic has made a *dent* in waiting times.

senses.gloss: A layer of a mineral or other substance that builds up naturally.
examples: The company found large copper *deposits* in the hills.
Hard water leaves white *deposits* in the kettle.
The river laid down a thick *deposit* of silt.

senses.gloss: Serious quality in someone's thought, feeling, or knowledge.
examples: Her essay has real *depth*.
He speaks about the region with unusual *depth* of knowledge.
The villain is entertaining but lacks *depth*.

senses.gloss: The family or nation that someone comes from.
examples: She is an American of Korean *descent*.
The name suggests French *descent*.
He traces his *descent* from a family of farmers.

senses.gloss: A slide into a worse condition.
examples: The book charts his *descent* into addiction.
The coup began the country's *descent* into chaos.
It was a slow *descent* from success into debt.

senses.gloss: A plan or drawing showing how something will be made or how it works.
examples: The *design* for the new bridge is on display at city hall.
Engineers changed the *design* after the crash tests.
Several *designs* were submitted for the memorial.

senses.gloss: The work of deciding how something will look and function.
examples: She studied graphic *design* in college.
Good *design* makes the app easy to use.
The company is known for careful *design*.

senses.gloss: A small group of soldiers or police given a particular job.
examples: The governor's security *detail* checked the room first.
A cleanup *detail* was sent down to the beach.
Two officers on his *detail* were injured.

senses.gloss: A technique a writer or speaker uses to create an effect.
examples: Repetition is a common *device* in speeches.
The novel uses a diary as a narrative *device*.
The poem relies on a few simple rhetorical *devices*.

senses.gloss: The choice of words a writer or speaker uses.
examples: The poem's plain *diction* makes it easy to read.
Her *diction* is formal, almost legal.
We were asked to compare the *diction* of the two speeches.

senses.gloss: A remark meant to mock or criticize someone.
examples: That comment was a *dig* at my cooking.
He got in a few *digs* about my driving.
She took a *dig* at her old boss during the interview.

senses.gloss: A finger or a toe.
examples: Frostbite can cost a climber several *digits*.
The surgeon reattached the severed *digit*.
Each hand has five *digits*.

senses.gloss: A person who is eating a meal in a restaurant.
examples: *Diners* were asked to leave when the alarm went off.
The waiter brought menus to the last two *diners*.
Most *diners* order the special.

senses.gloss: A short, high ringing sound.
examples: The elevator gave a soft *ding* at every floor.
I heard the *ding* of the microwave from upstairs.
Each message arrives with a little *ding*.

senses.gloss: A short swim.
examples: We took a *dip* in the lake before dinner.
A quick *dip* woke him right up.
The pool opens early for anyone who wants a morning *dip*.

senses.gloss: A temporary fall in an amount or level.
examples: Sales showed a small *dip* in February.
There was a sharp *dip* in temperature overnight.
The polls recorded a brief *dip* in support.

senses.gloss: A place where a road or the ground slopes down and back up.
examples: Slow down for the *dip* at the bottom of the hill.
The truck bottomed out in a *dip*.
A shallow *dip* in the field holds water after rain.

senses.gloss: An arrangement of things put out for people to look at.
examples: The store set up a holiday *display* in the window.
A *display* of local pottery filled the front hall.
The museum's dinosaur *display* is being rebuilt.

senses.gloss: A public show of something such as a skill or a feeling.
examples: The town puts on a fireworks *display* every July.
It was an ugly *display* of temper.
The team gave a fine *display* of passing.

senses.gloss: A written opinion by a judge who disagrees with the court's decision.
examples: The chief justice wrote a sharp *dissent*.
The ruling was six to three, with two separate *dissents*.
Her *dissent* has been quoted in later cases.

senses.gloss: A cheap, shabby bar or club.
examples: They played in every *dive* along the strip.
It's a *dive*, but the burgers are great.
The bar downstairs is a real *dive*.

senses.gloss: A raised platform where trucks are loaded and unloaded.
examples: The pallets are waiting on the loading *dock*.
Drivers back up to the *dock* to unload.
Deliveries come in through the *dock* in back.

senses.gloss: A stand that a phone, laptop, or other device sits in to charge or connect.
examples: He left his laptop in the *dock* at the office.
The speaker has a *dock* for your phone.
Both *docks* charge and transfer data at the same time.

senses.gloss: Someone who holds the highest university degree in a subject.
examples: She is a *doctor* of economics, not a physician.
After six years of research he finally became a *doctor*.
The lecture will be given by a *doctor* of history.

senses.gloss: An area of activity or knowledge that someone deals with.
examples: Tax law is outside my *domain*.
Robotics used to be the *domain* of a few big labs.
Each team works inside its own *domain*.

senses.gloss: The land or area that a ruler or an owner controls.
examples: The lord rode out across his *domain*.
That end of the park is the *domain* of skateboarders.
These waters are the *domain* of the coast guard.

senses.gloss: A person or group that gives money to a charity or a cause.
examples: The museum thanked its major *donors* at the dinner.
A single *donor* paid for the new wing.
The campaign lost several large *donors* after the scandal.

senses.gloss: Someone who lets other people treat them badly.
examples: Stop being a *doormat* and ask for a raise.
He let his brother walk all over him like a *doormat*.
She refused to be anyone's *doormat*.

senses.gloss: An amount of something that someone experiences.
examples: The trip gave us a healthy *dose* of reality.
Take his advice with a *dose* of skepticism.
A small *dose* of praise goes a long way.

senses.gloss: A person who looks exactly like someone else.
examples: You could be his *double*.
The actress met her *double* on the set.
In the photo the two men look like *doubles*.

senses.gloss: A hit in baseball that lets the batter reach second base.
examples: He drove in two runs with a *double* to left field.
She has ten *doubles* already this season.
A leadoff *double* started the rally.

senses.gloss: A drink with twice the usual amount of alcohol.
examples: He ordered a *double* after the meeting.
Make mine a *double*.
Two *doubles* on the rocks, please.

senses.gloss: A politician or official who prefers peace and negotiation to force.
examples: The debate split the cabinet into hawks and *doves*.
He was known as a *dove* on foreign policy.
Even the *doves* voted for the sanctions.

senses.gloss: In football, one of the four tries a team gets to advance the ball ten yards.
examples: It's third *down* and eight yards to go.
They picked up a first *down* on the next play.
The offense wasted two *downs* running out the clock.

senses.gloss: An early version of a piece of writing or a plan.
examples: The first *draft* of the report is due Friday.
He is on the fourth *draft* of the novel.
Lawyers reviewed a *draft* of the contract.

senses.gloss: A current of cool air moving through a room.
examples: There's a *draft* coming from under the door.
Close the window; I feel a *draft*.
Old houses are full of *drafts*.

senses.gloss: The system by which sports teams pick new players, or by which a country calls people into the army.
senses.ru: драфт (набор игроков); призыв на военную службу
examples: He was taken third overall in the *draft*.
Her grandfather was called up in the *draft*.
Both quarterbacks entered the *draft* a year early.

senses.gloss: Something boring or annoying.
examples: Waiting in line for two hours was a *drag*.
What a *drag* — the game got rained out.
Cleaning the garage is such a *drag*.

senses.gloss: A pull of smoke from a cigarette.
examples: He took a long *drag* and stared down the road.
She finished the cigarette in three *drags*.
One more *drag* and he put it out.

senses.gloss: Women's clothing worn by a man, especially for a performance.
examples: The show features six performers in *drag*.
He does *drag* on weekends under another name.
Half the cast appeared in *drag* for the finale.

senses.gloss: A game or contest that ends with the scores level.
examples: The match ended in a scoreless *draw*.
Two *draws* and a loss knocked them out of the tournament.
A *draw* was enough to keep the title.

senses.gloss: The choosing of names, teams, or prizes at random.
examples: The *draw* pits them against last year's champions.
Winners are picked in a weekly *draw*.
He got a tough *draw* in the first round.

senses.gloss: An event at which winning tickets or names are picked at random.
examples: The raffle *drawing* is at nine o'clock.
Nobody won Saturday's lottery *drawing*.
There are two *drawings* every week.

senses.gloss: Clothing of a particular kind or style.
examples: The invitation said formal *dress*.
The dancers wore traditional *dress*.
Casual *dress* is fine for the picnic.

senses.gloss: A pile of snow or sand heaped up by the wind.
examples: The plow pushed the *drifts* off the driveway.
Snow *drifts* buried the fence posts.
A *drift* of sand had blocked the trail.

senses.gloss: The general meaning of what someone is saying.
examples: I couldn't hear every word, but I caught his *drift*.
The *drift* of the meeting was that layoffs are coming.
He nodded as if he understood my *drift*.

senses.gloss: An exercise repeated so that people learn a skill or a routine.
examples: The school holds a fire *drill* every month.
The coach ran passing *drills* for an hour.
Spelling *drills* start the school day.

senses.gloss: The usual way that something is done.
examples: You know the *drill* — badge in, bag on the belt.
New hires learn the *drill* in about a week.
Same *drill* as last year, folks.

senses.gloss: A trip in a car.
examples: It's a two-hour *drive* to the coast.
We went for a *drive* along the river.
The *drive* home took forever in the snow.

senses.gloss: An organized effort to collect something or achieve a goal.
senses.ru: кампания, акция (по сбору средств и т. п.)
examples: The school is holding a canned food *drive*.
Their fundraising *drive* brought in half a million dollars.
Blood *drives* are held twice a year at the church.

senses.gloss: Energy and determination to get things done.
examples: She has the *drive* to build her own company.
He's talented but lacks *drive*.
Their *drive* carried the team through a bad season.

senses.gloss: A small program that lets a computer work with a piece of equipment.
examples: Download the printer *driver* from the website.
The scanner stopped working after a *driver* update.
The laptop installed the *drivers* automatically.

senses.gloss: The main cause of something happening or growing.
examples: Housing costs are the biggest *driver* of inflation here.
Tourism is the main *driver* of the local economy.
The report lists three *drivers* of the shortage.

senses.gloss: The golf club used to hit the ball farthest from the tee.
examples: He pulled out his *driver* on the long fifth hole.
Her *driver* sent the ball into the trees.
A new *driver* costs more than the rest of the bag.

senses.gloss: A thin stream of liquid poured over food.
examples: Finish the salad with a *drizzle* of olive oil.
The cake came with a *drizzle* of lemon glaze.
Add a *drizzle* of honey to the yogurt.

senses.gloss: A low, steady humming sound that goes on and on.
examples: The *drone* of the highway kept me awake.
He fell asleep to the *drone* of the lecture.
A steady *drone* came from the machine room.

senses.gloss: A male bee that does no work and cannot sting.
examples: The workers drive the *drones* out of the hive in the fall.
A *drone* exists only to mate with the queen.
*Drones* are stockier than worker bees.

senses.gloss: A long period without something that is needed or wanted.
examples: The team ended a nine-game scoring *drought*.
It's been a *drought* of good news around here.
The studio is coming off a two-year *drought* of hits.

senses.gloss: A large cylindrical container for oil, chemicals, or water.
examples: Rusting *drums* of fuel sat behind the shed.
The waste is shipped in sealed *drums*.
He cut a *drum* in half to make a grill.

senses.gloss: A narrow tube in the body that carries a fluid.
examples: Cold wind makes my tear *ducts* water.
The scan showed a blocked bile *duct*.
A small stone was lodged in the *duct*.

senses.gloss: A stupid person.
examples: Don't be a *dummy* — read the instructions.
I felt like a *dummy* for locking my keys in the car.
He called us *dummies* for believing him.

senses.gloss: A dirty, unpleasant, run-down place.
examples: The motel turned out to be a total *dump*.
I'm not eating in that *dump*.
They fixed up the old *dump* and sold it for a profit.
